etymologies.etymologyHTML: From cumulate +‎ -ive. Compare also French cumulatif, Italian cumulativo and Spanish cumulativo.

definitions.definition: Incorporating all current and previous data up to the present or at the time of measuring or collating.
That is formed by an accumulation of successive additions.

quote.citation: 1605, Francis Bacon, “(please specify |book=1 or 2)”, in The Twoo Bookes of Francis Bacon. Of the Proficience and Aduancement of Learning, Diuine and Humane, London:  […]  [Thomas Purfoot and Thomas Creede] for Henrie Tomes, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: As for knowledge which man receiveth by teaching, it is cumulative, not original.

quote.citation: 1850, Richard Chenevix Trench, Notes on the Miracles of Our Lord:
quote.text: The argument  […]  is in very truth not logical and single, but moral and cumulative.

definitions.definition: (finance) Having priority rights to receive a dividend that accrue until paid.
(law) (of evidence, witnesses, etc.) Intended to illustrate an argument that has already been demonstrated excessively.
